content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The record links the alcohol-policy violation to the reprimand and SOT through ROI cites (147, 248-9, 151), but the steps behind the pretext, similarly-situated and claim 5 findings are asserted in summary (e.g., 'assertions were not supported by preponderant evidence') without the underlying evidence being shown."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations carry ROI page cites and named roles (Witness 1, Medical Provider, management officials), but others such as 'witnesses reported' intoxication, 'no other officers who engaged in similar behavior,' and 'she provided no evidence' lack identified sources."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Key dates appear (Oct 24, 2020; Dec 3, 2020; May 5, 13, 14, 2021) but are out of order, the SOT on May 13 is reported after the May 14 reprimand, the dates for the EEO activity and the complaint filing are missing, and the dates for claims 1-11 are not laid out."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The record does not identify who decided the SOT, who reviewed the alcohol allegations, or what policy threshold applied, and the 'responsible management official' is unnamed; also unclear whether Complainant's denial was considered before the reprimand, since the denial is cited as a reason for the discipline."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Because the claims are numbered (claims 5, 9, 10; incidents 1-11) without being defined, the comparator and pretext findings rest on unsourced statements, and the decision-process and chronology are incomplete, an independent reviewer could not assess the decision on the merits without the full ROI."}}}
